phases.title: Discovery
phases.summary: Understand the business, its audience and its category before any visual decision is made.

pages.title: overview
pages.description: What this phase is for, what goes in and what must come out before strategy starts.

tip.title: principle
tip.text: Every design decision later must trace back to something written in this section.

blocks.label: Goal
blocks.text: Understand the business, its audience and its category before any visual decision is made.

blocks.label: Rule
blocks.text: No logos, colours or moodboards in this phase. Collect facts, not opinions.

blocks.label: Inputs
blocks.text: Client brief, stakeholder interviews, existing brand assets, analytics, customer reviews, sales material.

blocks.label: Activities
blocks.text:
1 Brief and kickoff
2 Stakeholder interviews
3 Audience research
4 Competitor and category review
5 Brand audit
6 Synthesis

blocks.label: Outputs
blocks.text: Discovery summary: problem, insights, opportunity, constraints, success criteria.

blocks.label: Done when
blocks.text: The client has read and approved the summary. It becomes the input for 02 strategy.

pages.title: client brief
pages.description: The reason the project exists and the rules of the engagement. Fill in during the kickoff call, then confirm in writing.

tip.title: how to
tip.text: Ask why at least twice. The first answer is the request, the second is the real problem.

blocks.label: Why now?
blocks.hint: What triggered this project: launch, growth, repositioning, merger, new market?

blocks.label: Business goal
blocks.hint: What must the brand help the business achieve? Tie it to a measurable outcome.

blocks.label: Success in 12 months
blocks.hint: How will we know the new brand works? Metrics, signals, perception shifts.

blocks.label: Scope and deliverables
blocks.hint: Identity, guidelines, website, packaging, motion, templates. What is in and what is out.

blocks.label: Budget and timeline
blocks.hint: Budget range, hard deadlines, launch date, key milestones.

blocks.label: Decision makers
blocks.hint: Who approves, who gives feedback, how many rounds, who has the final say.

blocks.label: Non-negotiables
blocks.hint: What must stay: name, colour, symbol, legal or technical constraints.

blocks.label: References
blocks.hint: Brands they admire and dislike, and why. Collect words, not just pictures.

pages.title: business
pages.description: What the company is, how it earns and where it is going. The brand has to fit the business it will serve in three years, not only today.

tip.title: how to
tip.text: Interview the founder, sales and support separately. Note where their answers disagree.

blocks.label: What do you sell?
blocks.hint: The offer in one plain sentence. No jargon.

blocks.label: Business model
blocks.hint: How the company makes money: pricing, channels, the margins that matter.

blocks.label: Origin story
blocks.hint: Why the company exists and what the founders believe.

blocks.label: Mission, vision, values
blocks.hint: Written or unwritten. Note what is real versus what is on the wall.

blocks.label: Unfair advantage
blocks.hint: What the business does better than anyone else, with proof.

blocks.label: 3 to 5 year plan
blocks.hint: New products, markets and audiences the brand must be able to stretch to.

blocks.label: Product architecture
blocks.hint: Products, services, sub-brands and how they relate.

blocks.label: Biggest challenge
blocks.hint: What is blocking growth today: awareness, trust, differentiation, price?

pages.title: audience
pages.description: Who the brand is for and what they need from it. Behaviour and context matter more than age and income.

tip.title: sources
tip.text: Customer interviews, reviews, support tickets, analytics, the sales team. Quote real words.

blocks.label: Primary audience
blocks.hint: Who they are: role, context, life stage. Behaviour over demographics.

blocks.label: Secondary audiences
blocks.hint: Partners, investors, talent, regulators. Anyone the brand must also speak to.

blocks.label: Jobs to be done
blocks.hint: What they are trying to get done when they come to this category.

blocks.label: Pains and frustrations
blocks.hint: What annoys them about the current options.

blocks.label: Motivations and triggers
blocks.hint: What makes them act, and what makes them hesitate.

blocks.label: How they choose
blocks.hint: Criteria, alternatives considered, who influences the decision.

blocks.label: Where attention lives
blocks.hint: Channels, communities, media and touchpoints they actually use.

blocks.label: Desired feeling
blocks.hint: How should they feel after meeting the brand? Three words maximum.

pages.title: competitors and category
pages.description: How the other players look, sound and position themselves. The goal is to find the codes of the category and the space nobody owns.

tip.title: how to
tip.text: Put all competitor logos, colours and homepages on one board. The cliches become obvious.

blocks.label: Category cliches
blocks.hint: Colours, symbols, words and layouts that everyone in the category uses.

blocks.label: White space
blocks.hint: Where the brand can look, sound or behave differently and still be credible.

pages.title: brand audit
pages.description: For rebrands only. An honest review of what exists today: what carries value and what holds the brand back.

tip.title: skip if
tip.text: The brand is new and has no assets in use. Go straight to the summary.

blocks.label: Asset inventory
blocks.hint: Logo, colour, type, imagery, iconography, voice, motion. Collect everything in use.

blocks.label: Brand equity
blocks.hint: What is recognisable and loved. Keep or evolve it, do not throw value away.

blocks.label: What is broken
blocks.hint: Inconsistent, outdated, illegible or impossible to apply.

blocks.label: Perception today
blocks.hint: How the team sees the brand versus how customers describe it.

blocks.label: Touchpoints reviewed
blocks.hint: Website, product, social, packaging, sales decks, signage, support.

blocks.label: Perception gap
blocks.hint:
From: how we are seen today.
To: how we need to be seen.

pages.title: discovery summary
pages.description: Everything above, reduced to one page the client signs. This page is the brief for 02 strategy.

tip.title: next
tip.text: 02 strategy: positioning, brand personality, tone of voice.

blocks.label: Problem to solve
blocks.hint: One sentence. If it takes a paragraph, discovery is not finished.

blocks.label: Key insights
blocks.hint: 3 to 5 findings about the business, audience and category that will drive decisions.

blocks.label: Opportunity
blocks.hint: The white space the brand can own.

blocks.label: Constraints and risks
blocks.hint: Budget, time, legal, technical, political.

blocks.label: Success criteria
blocks.hint: Agreed, measurable, signed off by the decision maker.

blocks.label: Sign-off
blocks.hint: Client name, date, approved to move to 02 strategy.

phases.title: Strategy
phases.summary: Turn what we learned into choices: who the brand is for, what it stands for and how it is different.

pages.title: purpose, vision, mission, values
pages.description: The foundation. Why the brand exists, where it is going and the principles it will not trade away.

tip.title: test
tip.text: If a competitor could sign the same sentence, it is not specific enough.

blocks.label: Purpose
blocks.hint: Why the brand exists beyond making money. One sentence.

blocks.label: Vision
blocks.hint: The future the brand wants to create. Where it will be in 5 to 10 years.

blocks.label: Mission
blocks.hint: What the brand does every day to get there, and for whom.

blocks.label: Value 01
blocks.hint: Name the value, then describe the behaviour that proves it.

blocks.label: Value 02
blocks.hint: Name the value, then describe the behaviour that proves it.

blocks.label: Value 03
blocks.hint: Name the value, then describe the behaviour that proves it.

pages.title: audience focus
pages.description: Strategy is a choice. From everyone in discovery, pick the one audience the brand is built for and the insight that unlocks them.

tip.title: source
tip.text: 01.3 audience. Use their real words wherever you can.

blocks.label: Core audience
blocks.hint: The one segment the brand is built for. Choosing is the point.

blocks.label: Not for
blocks.hint: Who we are willing to lose in order to be sharp.

blocks.label: Key insight
blocks.hint: A truth about the audience that the category ignores. I want this, but that gets in the way.

blocks.label: Need we answer
blocks.hint: The functional and emotional need the brand resolves.

blocks.label: Current belief
blocks.hint: What they think about the category or the brand today.

blocks.label: Desired belief
blocks.hint: What we want them to think after meeting the brand.

pages.title: positioning
pages.description: The place the brand owns in the mind of its audience, relative to the alternatives. The centre of the whole strategy.

tip.title: test
tip.text: Is it true? Does the audience care? Is it different from competitors? Can the business deliver it?

blocks.label: For
blocks.hint: The core audience from 02.2.

blocks.label: Who need
blocks.hint: The need or tension they have.

blocks.label: Brand is the
blocks.hint: Category or frame of reference people will compare it in.

blocks.label: That
blocks.hint: The single most important difference or benefit.

blocks.label: Because
blocks.hint: Reasons to believe. Three proofs the business can show.

blocks.label: Unlike
blocks.hint: The main alternative and what it fails to do.

blocks.label: Positioning statement
blocks.hint: For [audience] who [need], [brand] is the [category] that [difference], because [proof].

pages.title: brand idea
pages.description: One thought that holds the brand together. The bridge between strategy and design: identity, copy and behaviour all grow from it.

tip.title: test
tip.text: Can a designer start sketching from it? If not, it is still a description, not an idea.

blocks.label: Brand idea
blocks.hint: One thought in two to five words. The centre everything grows from.

blocks.label: What it means
blocks.hint: Two or three sentences that unpack the idea for the team.

blocks.label: Brand promise
blocks.hint: What people can always expect from the brand.

blocks.label: Brand story
blocks.hint: Short narrative: the world today, the tension, what the brand changes.

blocks.label: How it shows up
blocks.hint: Product, service, communication, behaviour. One example each.

blocks.label: Tagline options
blocks.hint: Optional. An external line that expresses the idea. Not the idea itself.

pages.title: brand personality
pages.description: If the brand were a person, who would walk into the room. Three to four traits, each with a limit so it does not become a caricature.

tip.title: format
tip.text: We are this, but never that. Confident, but never arrogant.

blocks.label: Trait 01
blocks.hint: We are [trait], but never [its extreme]. What it looks like in practice.

blocks.label: Trait 02
blocks.hint: We are [trait], but never [its extreme]. What it looks like in practice.

blocks.label: Trait 03
blocks.hint: We are [trait], but never [its extreme]. What it looks like in practice.

blocks.label: Trait 04
blocks.hint: We are [trait], but never [its extreme]. What it looks like in practice.

blocks.label: Archetype
blocks.hint: Optional shortcut. Use it as a prompt, not as the answer.

blocks.label: As a person
blocks.hint: How they dress, talk and behave in a room.

blocks.label: We are never
blocks.hint: Traits that would feel off-brand.

blocks.label: On the scales
blocks.hint: Playful or serious, modern or classic, loud or quiet, premium or accessible.

pages.title: tone of voice and messaging
pages.description: How the personality sounds in words, and what the brand says first. Write real sentences, not adjectives.

tip.title: how to
tip.text: Rewrite one existing headline in the new voice. If nothing changes, the principles are too vague.

blocks.label: Voice principle 01
blocks.hint: Name it, explain it, show one example sentence.

blocks.label: Voice principle 02
blocks.hint: Name it, explain it, show one example sentence.

blocks.label: Voice principle 03
blocks.hint: Name it, explain it, show one example sentence.

blocks.label: We say, we do not say
blocks.hint: Two real sentences side by side for each principle.

blocks.label: Core message
blocks.hint: The one thing people must remember.

blocks.label: Supporting messages
blocks.hint: Three proof-led messages for the core audience.

blocks.label: Vocabulary
blocks.hint: Words we own, words we avoid.

blocks.label: Tone by context
blocks.hint: How the voice flexes: website, social, support, error states.

pages.title: creative brief
pages.description: Strategy translated for design. The client signs this page, and every concept in 03 is judged against it instead of personal taste.

tip.title: next
tip.text: 03 visual identity: moodboards, concepts, logo, colour, type.

blocks.label: Strategy in one line
blocks.hint: Positioning and brand idea compressed into a single sentence.

blocks.label: Design should feel
blocks.hint: Three to five feelings the identity must evoke.

blocks.label: Design should never feel
blocks.hint: The feelings and category cliches to stay away from.

blocks.label: Evaluation criteria
blocks.hint: Three to five tests every concept will be judged against.

blocks.label: Must work on
blocks.hint: Priority touchpoints and smallest sizes: app icon, packaging, signage.

blocks.label: Mandatories
blocks.hint: Name, legal lines, assets to keep, accessibility requirements.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.hint: What 03 will produce, and in how many concept routes.

blocks.label: Sign-off
blocks.hint: Client name, date, approved to move to 03 visual identity.

pages.title: naming
pages.description: Only when the brand needs a new name. The name is the first expression of the brand idea, so it comes after strategy, not before.

tip.title: skip if
tip.text: The brand already has a name that stays.

blocks.label: Naming brief
blocks.hint: What the name must communicate and where it must work.

blocks.label: Criteria
blocks.hint: Short, pronounceable in key languages, ownable, fits the brand idea.

blocks.label: Territories
blocks.hint: Descriptive, suggestive, abstract, founder, coined. Explore several.

blocks.label: Long list
blocks.hint: Quantity first. Fifty or more before judging any.

blocks.label: Shortlist
blocks.hint: Three to five names, each with a rationale.

blocks.label: Checks
blocks.hint: Trademark, domain, social handles, meaning in other languages.

pages.title: brand architecture
pages.description: Only when there is more than one product or sub-brand. How the pieces of the portfolio relate, so the identity system can be built to scale.

tip.title: skip if
tip.text: The brand has one product and no sub-brands.

blocks.label: Portfolio today
blocks.hint: Every product, service and sub-brand that exists.

blocks.label: Model
blocks.hint: Branded house, endorsed brands, house of brands or hybrid.

blocks.label: Hierarchy
blocks.hint: Master brand, sub-brands, product names, descriptors.

blocks.label: Naming rules
blocks.hint: How new products get named.

blocks.label: Visual relationship
blocks.hint: How strongly each level borrows from the master brand.

blocks.label: Future additions
blocks.hint: What is planned and where it would sit.

phases.title: Identity
phases.summary: Give the strategy a face: a visual system that is distinctive, consistent and flexible across every touchpoint.

pages.title: visual territories
pages.description: Two or three distinct directions the identity could take, each grounded in the creative brief. Agree on a direction before drawing a logo.

tip.title: how to
tip.text: Mix type, colour, imagery and texture on each board. Avoid other logos, they anchor the client.

fields.label: Territory a
fields.hint: Name the direction in two or three words.

fields.label: Keywords
fields.hint: Three to five words this direction should feel like.

fields.label: Territory b
fields.hint: Name the direction in two or three words.

fields.label: Keywords
fields.hint: Three to five words this direction should feel like.

fields.label: Territory c
fields.hint: Name the direction in two or three words.

fields.label: Keywords
fields.hint: Three to five words this direction should feel like.

pages.title: concepts
pages.description: Two or three complete routes, not logo sketches. Each shows a logo, colour, type and at least one real application so it can be judged as a system.

tip.title: rule
tip.text: Never present a route you would not be happy to build. The client may pick it.

fields.label: Idea
fields.hint: How this route expresses the brand idea from 02.4.

fields.label: Against the brief
fields.hint: Score it on the evaluation criteria from 02.7. Strengths and risks.

fields.label: Idea
fields.hint: How this route expresses the brand idea from 02.4.

fields.label: Against the brief
fields.hint: Score it on the evaluation criteria from 02.7. Strengths and risks.

fields.label: Idea
fields.hint: How this route expresses the brand idea from 02.4.

fields.label: Against the brief
fields.hint: Score it on the evaluation criteria from 02.7. Strengths and risks.

pages.title: logo
pages.description: The chosen route refined into a logo system: every version needed to work from a favicon to a billboard.

tip.title: test
tip.text: Check it at 16 px, in one colour, on photo, on dark and next to competitors.

blocks.label: secondary lockup
blocks.hint: horizontal or stacked

blocks.label: Clear space and minimum size
blocks.hint: Unit of measure, exclusion zone, smallest size for print and screen.

blocks.label: Colour versions
blocks.hint: Full colour, one colour, reversed. Which backgrounds each one is for.

blocks.label: Misuse
blocks.hint: Do not stretch, recolour, outline, rotate or add effects. Show examples.

pages.title: colour
pages.description: A palette with clear roles. Fewer colours used with discipline are more recognisable than a wide palette.

tip.title: source
tip.text: 01.4 competitors. Choose where the category leaves space, not what is fashionable.

blocks.label: Proportions
blocks.hint: How much of each colour appears. Start from 60 / 30 / 10.

blocks.label: Accessibility
blocks.hint: Text and background pairs that pass WCAG AA contrast.

blocks.label: Meaning
blocks.hint: Why these colours, linked to the strategy and the brand idea.

pages.title: typography
pages.description: The voice of the brand in letters. One or two typefaces, a clear hierarchy and rules simple enough for a non-designer to follow.

tip.title: check
tip.text: Language support, licence for web and app, performance, a free fallback for documents.

blocks.label: type specimen
blocks.hint: Aa, alphabet, numerals, sample headline and paragraph

blocks.label: Primary typeface
blocks.hint: Name, foundry, weights in use. What it is used for.

blocks.label: Secondary typeface
blocks.hint: Optional. Only if it has a job the primary cannot do.

blocks.label: Hierarchy
blocks.hint: Display, heading, subheading, body, caption. Size, weight, line height.

blocks.label: Rules
blocks.hint: Case, alignment, tracking, maximum line length. What to avoid.

pages.title: imagery and graphic language
pages.description: Everything beyond logo, colour and type that makes the brand recognisable with the logo covered.

tip.title: test
tip.text: Hide the logo. Is it still clearly this brand?

blocks.label: photography
blocks.hint: examples of the right style

blocks.label: Photography
blocks.hint: Subject, light, colour grade, composition. What we never show.

blocks.label: illustration and icons
blocks.hint: examples and construction

blocks.label: Illustration and icons
blocks.hint: Style, stroke weight, corner radius, level of detail.

blocks.label: graphic language
blocks.hint: shapes, patterns, grid, motion

blocks.label: Graphic language
blocks.hint: Devices derived from the logo or idea. Layout grid and motion principles.

pages.title: applications
pages.description: The system tested on real touchpoints from the creative brief. This is where weak identities break and strong ones come alive.

tip.title: source
tip.text: 02.7 creative brief, must work on. Replace these six with the real priority touchpoints.

blocks.label: stationery
blocks.hint: business card, letterhead

blocks.label: website or app
blocks.hint: key screen

blocks.label: social media
blocks.hint: profile, post, story

pages.title: review and sign-off
pages.description: The identity checked against the strategy before it goes into guidelines. Judge by the agreed criteria, not by taste.

tip.title: next
tip.text: 04 guidelines and delivery: brand book, asset library, templates, handoff.

blocks.label: On strategy
blocks.hint: Does it express the positioning and brand idea? Point to where.

blocks.label: Distinctive
blocks.hint: Next to competitors, is it clearly different and ownable?

blocks.label: Works everywhere
blocks.hint: Small, large, one colour, light and dark, print and screen, motion.

blocks.label: Flexible system
blocks.hint: Can it produce new layouts without the designer in the room?

blocks.label: Accessible
blocks.hint: Contrast, legibility, colour not the only signal.

blocks.label: Sign-off
blocks.hint: Client name, date, approved to move to 04 guidelines and delivery.

phases.title: Guidelines
phases.summary: Turn the identity into a system the client can use without you: clear rules, complete files, ready templates.

pages.title: guideline structure
pages.description: Decide what kind of guideline this client needs before writing a page. A guide nobody opens protects nothing.

tip.title: principle
tip.text: Write for the least experienced person who will use it.

blocks.label: Audience
blocks.hint: Who will use it: marketing, agencies, developers, printers.

blocks.label: Format
blocks.hint: PDF, Figma file or web brand book. Where it lives and who can access it.

blocks.label: Depth
blocks.hint: One-page lite guide, standard guide or full brand book. Match the size of the client.

blocks.label: Chapters
blocks.hint: List the chapters this client actually needs. Cut the rest.

blocks.label: Writing style
blocks.hint: Short rules, real examples, do and do not. No essays.

blocks.label: Versioning
blocks.hint: Version number, date, owner, how changes are requested.

pages.title: brand guidelines
pages.description: The rules for every element from 03, written so that someone else can produce on-brand work. Tick off each chapter when it is written and illustrated.

tip.title: rule
tip.text: Every rule gets an example. Every do gets a do not.

items.label: Brand on a page: purpose, positioning, idea
Versions and when to use each

pages.title: asset library
pages.description: Every final file the client needs, exported, named and organised so that anyone can find the right logo in ten seconds.

tip.title: naming
tip.text: brand_asset_version_colour_format. Lowercase, no spaces, no final_v2.

items.label: Read me file at the top level

pages.title: templates
pages.description: Ready-to-use files for the priority touchpoints from the creative brief. Templates are where the brand survives day-to-day work.

tip.title: source
tip.text: 02.7 creative brief, must work on. Build only what the client will actually use.

items.label: Editable in the tools the client uses

pages.title: quality check
pages.description: The last pass before anything leaves your hands. Mistakes found by the client after delivery cost trust.

tip.title: test
tip.text: Give the package to someone outside the project. Ask them to make one layout using only the guide.

items.label: Vectors are clean, no stray points
Font licences cover the real use
An outsider made a layout with the guide
Gaps found in the test are fixed

pages.title: handover and launch
pages.description: Delivery is a moment, not an email with a link. Make sure the client team knows how to use the brand and who owns it from now on.

tip.title: how to
tip.text: Present the guide live, record the session and send the recording with the files.

blocks.label: Handover session
blocks.hint: Walk the client team through the guide and the files. Date and attendees.

blocks.label: Rights and ownership
blocks.hint: What is transferred, when, and what stays with the designer.

blocks.label: Rollout priorities
blocks.hint: What changes first, what waits. Old assets to retire.

blocks.label: Launch plan
blocks.hint: Internal reveal, external launch date, channels, announcement.

blocks.label: Brand owner
blocks.hint: The person on the client side who protects the brand after you leave.

blocks.label: Support period
blocks.hint: How long questions and small fixes are included, and what costs extra.

blocks.label: Final delivery
blocks.hint: Link to the package, date sent, confirmation received.

blocks.label: Sign-off
blocks.hint: Client name, date, project approved as complete.

pages.title: project close
pages.description: This page is for you, not the client. Capture the value of the project before moving to the next one.

tip.title: when
tip.text: Within a week of sign-off, while the details are fresh.

blocks.label: Case study
blocks.hint: Permission to publish, assets to prepare. Story: problem, idea, result.

blocks.label: Testimonial
blocks.hint: Ask the decision maker while the launch is fresh. One specific question works best.

blocks.label: Results to measure
blocks.hint: Return to the success criteria from 01. When and how to check them.

blocks.label: Retrospective
blocks.hint: What worked, what did not, where time was lost.

blocks.label: Process updates
blocks.hint: What to change in this template for the next project.

blocks.label: Next opportunities
blocks.hint: Retainer, website, campaign, brand check-in after six months.
